content:
Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic forecast errors and derive correction rules.

## Example 1: 2024-09-12
- History: Price dropped from 73+ to 66.40 range over 18 days
- Sentiment: Mixed, starting positive (1.00) then becoming more negative
- Model forecast: Starts at 65.64, gradually increasing to 61.67
- True outcome: Starts at 65.45, gradually increasing to 64.89

Looking at the differences:
- Model is consistently ~0.2-0.3 lower than true outcomes
- Both show clear upward trend in both forecast and true values
- The model underestimates the true prices by about 3-5% consistently

## Example 2: 2024-09-13
- Very similar to Example 1, just 1 day later
- Model forecasts start at 65.40, true outcomes at 64.99
- Again, model is slightly lower but the gap varies
- Looking more closely: model forecasts seem to lag the true outcomes slightly

## Example 3: 2024-09-11
- Almost identical to Example 1 (just the last data point changed)
- Model forecasts: [66.33, 65.56, ...]
- True outcomes: [66.40, 65.45, ...]

Let me look at the pattern more carefully across all examples:

## Example 4: 2024-05-07
- History: Prices in the 66-74 range, no clear downtrend
- Sentiment: Starts positive (1.00), becomes more mixed
- Model forecasts: [71.07, 71.87, 72.98, ...]
- True outcomes: [70.85, 71.92, 73.62, ...]

Looking at the first few points:
- Model predicts 71.07, true is 70.85 (error +0.22, +0.3%)


- Model predicts 71.87, true is 71.92 (error -0.05, -0.1%)
- Model predicts 72.98, true is 73.62 (error -0.64, -0.9%)

I notice the model tends to underpredict when sentiment is positive, especially at longer forecast horizons. The discrepancies appear to correlate with sentiment shifts, particularly when moving from initial positive
